Hit this on 1.18.13 and dug into it — posting the root cause, since it's a bit more specific than the title suggests and I don't think #38372 as it stands fully closes it.

Two things combine.

`packages/app/src/pages/session/composer/prompt-model-selection.ts` orders the persisted draft model ahead of the agent's:

```ts
const key = [prompt.model.current(), input.agent()?.model, configured(), recent(), fallback()].find(
  (item): item is ModelKey => !!item && valid(item),
)
```

And `openNewTab` in `packages/app/src/components/titlebar.tsx` seeds a new draft with the previous tab's model:

```ts
const model = tabs.stateValue<PromptSession>(sessionTab, "prompt")?.model.current()
tabs.newDraft({ server: sessionTab.server, directory: activeSession.directory }, "", model)
```

So the wrong model is already in the draft before the agent is ever consulted. #38372 hooks the agent select callback, which covers step 3 of the repro here — but a new tab opened without touching the agent picker still starts on the inherited model, because the select never fires.

Worth flagging: #39319 is the same code path from the opposite side, where the agent's model overwriting a manual pick is the complaint. A fix that just makes the agent model win harder will reopen that one.

What worked for me is scoping rather than reordering: tag the persisted selection with the agent it was made under, and only honour it while that agent is active. Values without a tag — pre-existing drafts, and models inherited via `openNewTab` — lose to a configured agent model, but are still honoured for agents that have no model configured, so the inheritance behaviour stays intact where it's unambiguous.

That gives:

- new session and agent switch land on the agent's model (this issue)
- a manual pick survives across turns while you stay on that agent (#39319)
- switching away and back restores it

I've been running this against 1.18.13 as a patched bundle rather than a source build. Happy to open a PR against `dev` if that direction looks right.

Dropping the keywords fixes the API error but leaves some tools undocumented to the model. The real-world case that led me here is the hosted Notion MCP, whose `notion-create-attachment` tool has a *pure* top-level `anyOf`: three branches and no top-level `properties` at all (makenotion/notion-mcp-server#340). After the drop the model sees `{"type": "object"}` and has to guess every argument.

Suggestion: merge the branches instead of dropping them.

- `properties`: union across branches (first definition wins on collision)
- `required`: intersection for `anyOf`/`oneOf`, union for `allOf`
- append the valid combinations to the description, e.g. `Exactly one of these parameter combinations must be provided: filename + content; or filename + source_url; or source_file_id.`

I run this as a local sanitizing proxy today and the merged schema works well with Anthropic models; the description line is enough for the model to pick a valid branch. I can send the merge logic as a follow-up if this PR wants to stay minimal.

Additional data point, now reproduced **upstream at the official DeepSeek API** (api.deepseek.com with a first-party key), independent of the OpenCode gateway: see #40607. Same self-identification (V3.x, cutoff 2024-07/2025-05) on 3/3 attempts, Chinese and English.

Two notes to strengthen the evidence beyond self-identification:

1. **Official endpoint, not OpenCode**: the responses come straight from api.deepseek.com with `model: "deepseek-v4-flash"`. If the official API itself is still routing to a legacy alias, then Zen/Go pass-through is not the root cause (or at least not the only one) — worth verifying with DeepSeek directly.

2. **Hard config difference (not self-report)**: `opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free` is capped at **200K context** in models.dev metadata (`context: 200000`), and the server rejects inputs >163,840 tokens with an explicit error (#35991) — vs the official 1M context on paid `deepseek-v4-flash`. The free tier was also reduced from ~1M to 200K at some point (#27929). This is a measurable, non-self-reported difference.

Acknowledging the "self-identification isn't proof" caveat — agreed, but combined with the context cap and the official-endpoint reproduction, it points to a checkpoint/routing mismatch rather than a quantization difference (neither model has any quantization marker in models.dev data or the Zen schema; official V4 Flash weights are natively FP4+FP8 QAT anyway).

This would be really valuable - with a lot of skills installed the context cost adds up fast, and manual-only skills are the obvious thing to cut.

I've implemented it in #40609: skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` are still discovered and still invocable as `/skill-name`, but they're left out of `<available_skills>` and the `skill` tool refuses to load them. Covered in both the v1 and v2 skill paths, with tests.

Happy to adjust the approach if maintainers want it done differently.

Stamping the other events was the right call: I'd optimised for the smallest diff and left the schema half-and-half, where `step_finish` said the model and `text` didn't. It's now on `step_start`, `step_finish`, `text`, `reasoning` and `tool_use`, with the lookup hoisted once per part. The attribution test runs a non-default model through a tool call so it covers all four event types in one run.

`agent` is in too, though not for the reason you gave — worth flagging in case it bit you elsewhere. Subagent turns can't show up on this stream: the `task` tool runs the subagent in a child session (`sessionID: nextSession.id`, `tool/task.ts:204`) and the loop drops anything that isn't the current session (`if (part.sessionID !== sessionID) continue`). So a parent turn and a subagent turn are never both in this output.

What does make it useful is the parent's own agent varying — `--agent plan` vs `build` — and the default format already printing agent and model together. Verified live: with `--agent plan` every event reports `agent: plan`.

**[SUPERSEDED]** — See [this comment](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36181#issuecomment-5190119002) for the verified conclusion (direct SSH testing): the 401 in our environment is **serve's own HTTP Basic Auth gate** (client lacked `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`), and `auth.json` was intact and its key valid. The "auth.json not loaded" framing below is retracted; the `auth.json` path claims were also corrected in [this comment](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36181#issuecomment-5190023452).

---

Adding a data point from our deployment: this issue also affects **`opencode serve` (headless server mode)** after a process restart, not only new TUI sessions.

**Environment**
- Ubuntu 22.04 (headless server), `opencode serve` running as a systemd **user** service, listening on port 4096
- Binary version: `1.18.13_F050429` (custom fork build)
- Restart time: 2026-08-05 16:13 CST

**Symptoms**
- After restarting the `opencode serve` process, every LLM request returns `401 Unauthorized` — the provider credentials in `auth.json` are not loaded by the new process.
- `auth.json` exists at both candidate paths and holds the expected provider entries (no corruption observed):
  - `/root/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`
  - `/root/.config/opencode/auth.json`
- In serve mode there is no interactive `/connect` to re-authenticate, so the 401 state persists until the process is externally stopped/reconfigured.

This looks like the same "auth.json not loaded on startup" root cause as described here, manifesting in serve mode instead of a new TUI session. The concurrent-write race referenced in #30396 also seems plausible as a root cause for a restart scenario. Happy to run a debug build or capture startup logs if that helps narrow it down.

**Correction to my previous comment** (facts verified on the server, 2026-08-05):

Some details in my earlier comment were not accurate. Verified facts below:

- **auth.json**: only `/root/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` exists (202 bytes, JSON is valid, contains two provider entries: `deepseek`, `moonshotai-cn`). `/root/.config/opencode/auth.json` does **not** exist — my earlier "exists at both candidate paths" was wrong.
- **Service start time**: systemd reports `ExecMainStartTimestamp = 2026-08-05 16:57:22 CST` for the running `opencode.service` (MainPID 369912). I could not verify a restart at 16:13 CST.
- **Current 401 reproduction** (via direct localhost curl, bypassing the machine's outbound proxy): `GET http://127.0.0.1:4096/v1/models` → `401` with empty body; also `401` when sending `Authorization: Bearer <OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD>` and `x-opencode-token`. I cannot yet tell whether this 401 comes from serve's own password gate or from provider auth not being loaded — the auth header format for the serve API is not confirmed.
- **Binary**: `1.18.13_F050429` at `/root/.opencode/bin/opencode` (note: `F050429` looks like a custom build marker).

I'll update this comment if I can pin down whether the 401 is caused by `auth.json` not being loaded (the root cause this issue is about) versus serve's own auth gate.

**Final verification result** (direct SSH test on the server, 2026-08-05, per my earlier "I'll update this comment"):

The 401 we hit is **serve's own HTTP Basic Auth gate, not an auth.json loading problem**.

Layer-by-layer curl results (all against the running `opencode serve` on port 4096):

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/models` (no auth) | `401` |
| `GET /v1/models` with `Authorization: Basic base64(opencode:<OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD>)` | `200` |
| `GET /` with same Basic auth | `200` |
| `GET /app` with same Basic auth | `200` |
| `GET https://api.deepseek.com/models` with the API key from `auth.json` (Bearer) | `200` |

`auth.json` (`/root/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`, the only path opencode reads — it uses `Global.Path.data/auth.json`) is intact (providers: `deepseek`, `moonshotai-cn`) and the stored key is valid against the provider API. `opencode serve` authenticates correctly once the client sends the Basic credentials.

So in our environment the observed 401 is the password gate rejecting an unauthenticated client — **not** a case of "auth.json not loaded on startup" as this issue describes. The earlier guesses in my first comment (and the plausible-cause framing) should be disregarded. If a client starts getting 401 after a serve restart, the more likely cause is that the client process does not have `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` set/matching the server's (the password inside a systemd unit is not automatically passed on to client processes), not that `auth.json` was dropped.

### Workarounds (confirmed working on the affected machine)

**Quick fix — make opencode find `rg.exe` without downloading:**

opencode resolves ripgrep in this order: `which("rg.exe")` → `<Global.Path.bin>/rg.exe` → download from GitHub (`packages/core/src/ripgrep/binary.ts`). On Windows, `Global.Path.bin` is `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\opencode\bin\`. So:

1. Download ripgrep for Windows: `gh release download 15.1.0 --repo BurntSushi/ripgrep --pattern "ripgrep-15.1.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip"`
2. Extract it and copy `rg.exe` to `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\opencode\bin\rg.exe` (create the directory if needed)
3. **Restart opencode** — required because of Bug 2 (the failed resolution is cached in the process; only a fresh process will pick up the binary)

**Root-cause fix — fix the PowerShell module resolution:**

The failure only happens because Windows PowerShell 5.1 inherits the MSIX PowerShell 7 session's `PSModulePath`, which lists the Store package's `$PSHOME\Modules` (Core-only modules) before `C:\Windows\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules\`. The 5.1 autoloader stops at the first incompatible (Core-only) match and reports `CouldNotAutoloadMatchingModule` instead of continuing the search.

Options:

- **Recommended:** uninstall the Microsoft Store (MSIX) version of PowerShell 7 and install the official **MSI** distribution instead (same consensus as #17372 and #20603). MSI PowerShell 7 keeps `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\` out of the 5.1 module-search collision and is serviced by Windows Update.
- Alternatively, launch opencode from Windows PowerShell 5.1 or from a terminal that does not put the MSIX pwsh package dir ahead of `system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules\` in `PSModulePath`.

**Verification:**

- `rg.exe` alone fixes grep/glob permanently — confirmed on the affected machine after restart (headless `opencode run` returned 64 matches; in-session grep returned 18 matches).
- The node repro confirmed the env dependence: spawning 5.1 with the full MSIX-inherited `PSModulePath` reproduces the exact `CouldNotAutoloadMatchingModule` error; removing/overriding `PSModulePath` makes extraction succeed.

Reproduction (OpenCode 1.18.x on macOS):
1. Open the install-plugin command palette in the TUI.
2. Type `o`, then `h`, then Enter.

Verified ground truth from my session:
- `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` had `"oh"` appended under `plugin` after the picker accepted it. Backup of the same minute at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json.bak.20260805-165433` shows the entry was written before any UI re-prompt.
- `sndrs/oh@0.2.1-2` is the only npm package literally named `oh`, so the picker's "narrow down to one match" heuristic deterministically picks it.
- `sndrs/oh`'s `package.json` exposes `main: index.js` and `bin: bin/oh`; it has no `opencode` plugin field. Persisting it into the OpenCode plugin list breaks the next launch.

This is the same bug #33749 reports, just triggered from the TUI picker instead of CLI argument tokens. The picker:
1. Searches the entire npm registry (no scope/keyword/`opencode`-field filtering, no curated OpenCode-plugin list).
2. Has no second confirmation step before `npm install` runs.
3. Persists the installed package into the user's plugin manifest without validating that it's actually an OpenCode plugin shape.

I also see that `packages/opencode/src/permission/arity.ts` already declares a `wp: 2` write-permission entry for `plugin install`. The picker appears to bypass that flow because it runs as a named command rather than a bash invocation; routing it through the existing `wp` flow would close the gap.
